questions.q: You changed products.py. What is the right order to save that change as a commit?
options: git add products.py, then git commit -m "Add Steel Water Bottle to the catalog"
questions.explain: git add puts the change on the stage (you choose it); git commit saves everything on the stage as a new commit.

options: Because .env holds secrets like the database password, and anything committed stays in the history forever
So that git log is shorter
questions.explain: Files listed in .gitignore are never saved by Git. A committed secret is in every copy of the history, so it must be changed at once.

questions.q: In git diff, what does a line starting with + mean?
questions.explain: + lines were added, - lines were removed. Lines with a space in front didn't change; they show where you are.

questions.q: git commit prints: no changes added to commit (use "git add" and/or "git commit -a"). What happened?
options: You changed a file but didn't git add it, so the stage was empty and nothing was saved
The commit message was too short
questions.explain: Git commits only what's on the stage. Run git add products.py, then commit again.

options: Fix checkout crash when the cart is empty
I fixed some stuff in checkout today and also other things
questions.explain: Short, written like an order ("Fix ..."), and it says what and when. One commit = one logical change.

questions.q: You broke products.py by mistake and haven't committed. How do you get back the version from the last commit?
questions.explain: git restore copies the file back from the last commit. Careful: your uncommitted changes to that file are lost for good.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Neha committed .env yesterday, and the team already has that commit. What should she do first?
options: Delete .env and commit; the password is safe now
Change the database password, because it is in the history now
questions.explain: A new commit doesn't remove the old one: the password stays in the history. Change the secret first; then stop tracking the file (git rm --cached .env) and add it to .gitignore.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Where does Git keep the staging area?
questions.explain: The stage is a single file, .git/index. Commits and file versions live in .git/objects, named by their hashes.
